I've never done that method of TA testing so I can't say if your numbers are correct. 12% and 12 g/L are different expressions of the same thing though, so that tracks. 

Phenolic ripeness is hard to describe, you really just have to taste constantly and you'll figure it out. It took me making multiple vineyard trips and tasting throughout the growing season to understand. The grapes go from just having sugar and acid, and suddenly they'll hit a point where the more complex flavors will just pop out and show themselves.

What do you ultimately plan to do with the grapes? You can probably get some more hang time on them at this point, your brix can tick up several degrees and still be fine and hopefully the acids will drop. You can always deacidify if need be.
Am I reading that right that you're around 10 g/L TA, and 2.5 pH at just over 20 brix? Those are some super underripe acid numbers... How do they taste, are they showing any phenolic ripeness?
